extracted.intended_audience: users and programmers of the Singular computer algebra system (Singular CAS)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference list / TOC entries describing common tricks, pitfalls, limitations, and language differences when writing code for the Singular computer algebra system. Useful for programmers porting code or learning language-specific behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tricks and pitfalls
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading listing common tricks and pitfalls when using the system (section 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an umbrella for subsections on limitations, system-dependent issues, language differences to C, miscellaneous oddities, and identifier resolution. Detailed explanations are in the referenced subsections (not included in this TOC chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates there are inherent limits to the system's capabilities; specifics are in section 6.1 of the manual (text not present in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: System dependent limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that some limitations depend on the host system or environment; see section 6.2 for platform-specific caveats (details not in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major differences to the C programming language
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6.3 — Enumerates important differences between Singular's language and C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This heading introduces several specific language-behavior differences (6.3.1–6.3.8); consult those subitems for concrete rules when porting or writing code.

rubrics_metrics.name: No rvalue of increments and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6.3.1 — No rvalue of increments and assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that increment/assignment expressions do not yield rvalues (i.e., they cannot be used as expressions producing values) in Singular. Full examples and implications are in the body of section 6.3.1 (not included here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of logical expressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flags that logical expressions may be evaluated differently than in C (short-circuiting, truth values, etc.); concrete semantics and examples are in section 6.3.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: No case or switch statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6.3.3 — There is no case or switch statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that the language lacks C-style case/switch constructs; developers must use alternative control structures. See section 6.3.3 for recommended patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage of commas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates commas behave differently or have language-specific restrictions; consult section 6.3.4 for exact rules and anti-patterns (TOC only here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage of brackets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes special or nonstandard bracket/parenthesis usage rules compared to C; examples and rules are in section 6.3.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of continue
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies how the continue statement behaves in Singular (may differ from C); see section 6.3.6 for exact semantics and edge cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return type of procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how procedure return types are handled (typing, defaults, restrictions); details and examples in section 6.3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: First index is 1
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents that array/matrix indexing in Singular is 1-based (the first index equals 1), unlike C's 0-based indexing; see section 6.3.8 for implications when porting code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous oddities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects assorted nonstandard or surprising behaviors of the language or system; consult section 6.4 for concrete items and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Section heading — Identifier resolution (appears after miscellaneous oddities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to rules about how identifiers are found/resolved in scope/environment; the detailed resolution rules are in the full manual text (not included in this chunk).
